{"path":"/study","markdown":"# Verification report: lid-driven-cavity

foam-verify 0.0.1, from `study.toml`: 4 levels, finest first; refined = mesh; grid sequence structured; refined directions d = 2; formal order 2.

## Verdict

**Not a clean pass.** 0 of 1 quantity of interest are clean passes.

| QoI | Finest grid | Relative U | Grid convergence | Clean pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `u(y=0.5)` | -0.208691 +/- 0.000234 | 0.11% | monotonic, p = 2.407 | no |

What stops a clean pass:

- `u(y=0.5)`: level 160x160: drifting: over the last 20 samples (x = 0.05 to 1): relative range 0.712, relative drift -0.485; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing

## Levels

| Level | Folder | Cells | r to the next coarser |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160x160 | `n160` | 25,600 | 2.000 |
| 80x80 | `n80` | 6,400 | 2.000 |
| 40x40 | `n40` | 1,600 | 2.000 |
| 20x20 | `n20` | 400 |  |

## Settings consistency

**Pass.** No difference blocks a clean pass; the differences below are noted.

Compared on every level: `system/fvSchemes`, `system/fvSolution`, `constant/transportProperties`, `0/U`, `0/p`, `system/controlDict`.

| File | Entry | 160x160 | 80x80 | 40x40 | 20x20 | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `system/controlDict` | `endTime` | 1 | 10 | 10 | 10 | no |
| `system/controlDict` | `deltaT` | 0.0003125 | 0.000625 | 0.00125 | 0.0025 | no |
| `system/controlDict` | `writeInterval` | 1 | 10 | 10 | 10 | no |

## `u(y=0.5)`

**Not a clean pass.** -0.208691 +/- 0.000234 (GCI, 0.11%); band -0.208926 to -0.208457.

From `postProcessing/ghiaPoints/*/U`, column `0`, x component, last value; window: the last 10% of the samples, at least 50.

| Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Grid convergence | pass | grids 1-3: convergence ratio R = 0.1886: monotonic convergence (0 < R < 1) |
| Refinement ratio | pass | r21 = 2.000, r32 = 2.000; at least 1.3 (Celik et al. 2008, step 2) |
| Observed order | pass | p = 2.407 (closed form, equal ratios), within [0.5, 4] for a formal order of 2; Fs = 1.25; U uses p = 2, the formal order (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4) |
| Asymptotic range | pass | GCI_32 / (r21^p GCI_21) = 1.003, within [0.9, 1.1] |
| Coarser triplets | pass | grids 2-4: monotonic, p = 1.867 |
| Iterative convergence | fail | drifting on 160x160; converged on 80x80, 40x40, 20x20; warnings on 160x160 (tol 0.001) |
| Iterative error | pass | largest u_it / U = 2.1e-09 (40x40), within 1/100 (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4) |
| Settings consistency | pass | no difference blocks (6 files compared); noted: system/controlDict endTime, system/controlDict deltaT, system/controlDict writeInterval |
| Refined directions | pass | dim = 2, with empty or wedge patches on every level: frontAndBack |
| Refinement scope | assumed | scope mesh: assumes every cell, near-wall layers included, was refined by the same ratio (Celik et al. 2008, step 2: systematic refinement, geometrically similar cells) |
| Grid sequence | assumed | grid sequence structured: the levels refine one base grid systematically (the base grid may itself be unstructured), so Fs = 1.25 with three or more grids (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1) |

| Level | Value | Iterative | Window | Relative range | Relative drift | u_it | u_it / U |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 160x160 | -0.2086913 | drifting | 20 of 20, 0.05 to 1 | 0.71 | -0.48 |  |  |
| 80x80 | -0.2081288 | converged | 50 of 200, 7.55 to 10 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 40x40 | -0.2051463 | converged | 50 of 200, 7.55 to 10 | 4.9e-12 | 1.1e-12 | 5.0e-13 | 2.1e-09 |
| 20x20 | -0.1942651 | converged | 50 of 200, 7.55 to 10 | 5.1e-12 | -1.7e-12 | 5.0e-13 | 2.1e-09 |

Richardson extrapolation, grids 1-3 (at the observed order; U uses p = 2): phi_ext = -0.2088221, e_a = 0.27%, e_ext = 0.063%, GCI_fine = 0.078%, GCI_32 = 0.42%, Fs = 1.25.

| Grids | Convergence | Result | Relative U |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-3 | monotonic, p = 2.407 | -0.208691 +/- 0.000234 | 0.11% |
| 2-4 | monotonic, p = 1.867 | -0.20813 +/- 0.00141 | 0.68% |

Notes:

- observed order p = 2.407 is above the formal order 2, so the uncertainty uses p = 2 (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4); the Richardson numbers and the asymptotic-range check use the observed p
- 4 grids: one result per consecutive triplet; the verdict is from grids 1-3.

## Method

- Grid convergence after Celik et al. (2008), with the convergence types of Eça and Hoekstra (2014): Fs = 1.25 on three or more grids of a structured grid sequence, and 3 for an unstructured sequence (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1), on two grids, or when p is outside [0.5, 4]; refinement ratios of at least 1.3; an asymptotic-range ratio within [0.9, 1.1]; with four or more grids, every coarser triplet converges monotonically too. Above the formal order, U uses the formal order (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4); the Richardson numbers and the checks keep the observed p. An oscillatory triplet gets a spread bound and never a clean pass (foam-verify docs/gci.md).
- Iterative convergence of each QoI from its own history over the window given with it: converged when its relative range and relative drift are within tol, and u_it is half the range. On the grids behind the result, u_it must be at most U/100 (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4; docs/iterative.md).
- Settings consistency: the schemes, solver settings, physical properties, boundary conditions and near-wall layer settings of the levels, compared entry by entry (docs/consistency.md).
- U is the uncertainty of the finest-grid value, and the band is that value +/- U. A QoI is a clean pass only when no check fails (docs/report.md).
"}

content.text:
**No, it isn't converged.** The grid study looks fine on paper, but the finest grid's value is not a steady-state result, so I can't give a trustworthy uncertainty.

**Why:**
- **The finest grid stopped too early.** The 160x160 case has `endTime` 1, while the other three levels ran to 10. Its value of u(y=0.5) was still changing when the run stopped. Over its last 20 samples (t = 0.05 to 1), the relative range is 0.71 and the relative drift is −0.48, far above the 0.001 tolerance. The 80x80, 40x40 and 20x20 levels have all settled, with drift of about 1e-12 or less.
- **The grid numbers rest on that value.** The study reports −0.208691 ± 0.000234 (0.11%), with monotonic convergence and observed order p = 2.41. Every other check passes. But the ±0.000234 is only as good as the finest-grid value. With a drift that large, the iterative error almost certainly outweighs the stated grid uncertainty, so that band means nothing.
- **The coarser grids can't stand in for it.** Grids 2–4 converge monotonically (p = 1.87) and give −0.20813 ± 0.00141. That is the 80x80 value, not the finest grid's, so it doesn't answer your question. It's only a rough guide.

**To fix it:** rerun `n160` with `endTime` 10 (and `writeInterval` to match), the same as the other levels, then rerun the verification.

FINAL: converged=no; value=-0.208691; uncertainty=none
